question: What does the manual say is the most important reason for doing a vehicle inspection?
choice_a: Safety for yourself and other road users
choice_b: To avoid fines from state inspectors
choice_c: To satisfy the motor carrier's insurance company
choice_d: To keep the vehicle's resale value high
explanation: The manual states, "Safety is the most important reason you inspect your vehicle, safety for yourself and for other road users."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.1 Vehicle Inspection

question: According to the manual, what is the minimum tread depth required in every major groove on front tires?
explanation: The manual states, "You need at least 4/32-inch tread depth in every major groove on front tires."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.1 Vehicle Inspection

question: What is the minimum tread depth required on tires other than the front tires?
explanation: The manual states, "You need 2/32 inch on other tires."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.1 Vehicle Inspection

question: How much steering wheel play is considered excessive and can make a vehicle hard to steer?
explanation: The manual states, "Steering wheel play of more than 10 degrees (approximately 2 inches movement at the rim of a 20-inch steering wheel) can make it hard to steer."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.1 Vehicle Inspection

question: A leaf spring will be placed "out of service" if what portion of its leaves are missing or broken?
explanation: The manual states, "Missing or broken leaves in any leaf spring. If one-fourth or more are missing, it will put the vehicle 'out of service'."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.1 Vehicle Inspection

question: During the in-cab inspection, air pressure should build from 50 psi to 90 psi within approximately how many minutes?
explanation: The manual states, "Pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.1 Vehicle Inspection

question: Drivers of trucks and truck tractors transporting cargo must inspect the cargo securement within the first how many miles of a trip?
explanation: The manual requires inspecting cargo securement "within the first 50 miles of a trip and every 150 miles or every three hours (whichever comes first) after."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.1 Vehicle Inspection

question: When testing a hydraulic brake system for leaks, how long should you hold firm pressure on the brake pedal?
explanation: The manual states, "Then apply firm pressure to the pedal and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.1 Vehicle Inspection

question: When backing a vehicle, the manual recommends backing and turning toward which side whenever possible?
choice_c: Either side, it makes no difference
choice_d: The side with the most mirrors
explanation: The manual states, "Back and Turn Toward the Driver's Side... so that you can see better. Backing toward the right side is very dangerous because you can't see as well."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.2 Basic Control of Your Vehicle

question: What gear should you use when backing a vehicle, according to the manual?
choice_d: Whatever gear was last used driving forward
explanation: The manual states, "Back Slowly. Always back as slowly as possible. Use the lowest reverse gear."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.2 Basic Control of Your Vehicle

question: How should your hands be positioned on the steering wheel for safe control?
choice_a: Both hands close together at the top of the wheel
choice_b: One hand at the bottom, one at the top
choice_c: Hands on opposite sides of the wheel
choice_d: Only one hand is needed if the other operates controls
explanation: The manual states, "Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands. Your hands should be on opposite sides of the wheel."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.2 Basic Control of Your Vehicle

question: What should you do when accelerating in poor traction conditions such as rain or snow?
choice_a: Accelerate hard to power through the slick spot
choice_c: Apply the parking brake while accelerating
explanation: The manual states, "Speed up very gradually when traction is poor, as in rain or snow. If you use too much power, the drive wheels may spin."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.2 Basic Control of Your Vehicle

question: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require what technique to change gears?
explanation: The manual states, "Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require double clutching to change gears."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.3 Shifting Gears

question: According to the manual, when should you downshift before starting down a hill?
choice_a: Only after the vehicle begins to speed up
choice_b: Before starting down the hill, to a speed you can control without using the brakes hard
choice_c: While already braking hard partway down
choice_d: Only if the hill has a posted grade sign
explanation: The manual states, "Slow down and shift down to a speed that you can control without using the brakes hard... Downshift before starting down the hill."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.3 Shifting Gears

question: Why does the manual recommend downshifting before entering a curve?
choice_b: It is required by law on all curves
choice_c: It lets you use some power through the curve to help the vehicle be more stable
choice_d: It prevents the turn signal from canceling early
explanation: The manual states, "This lets you use some power through the curve to help the vehicle be more stable while turning."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.3 Shifting Gears

question: When should you turn off a retarder, according to the manual?
choice_d: Whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow-covered
explanation: The manual states, "You should turn the retarder off whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow covered," because poor traction can cause the drive wheels to skid.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.3 Shifting Gears

question: On vehicles with automatic transmissions, why is selecting a low range important when going down grades?
choice_a: It gets greater engine braking and prevents the transmission from shifting up beyond the selected gear
choice_c: It automatically applies the parking brake
explanation: The manual states, "You can select a low range to get greater engine braking going down grades. The lower ranges prevent the transmission from shifting up beyond the selected gear."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.3 Shifting Gears

question: Most good drivers look ahead how many seconds' worth of travel distance?
explanation: The manual states, "Most good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.4 Seeing

question: At highway speeds, looking 12 to 15 seconds ahead corresponds to about how much distance?
explanation: The manual states, "At highway speeds it's about a quarter of a mile," while at lower speeds it's about one block.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.4 Seeing

question: When should mirror adjustment be checked, according to the manual?
choice_c: Once a year during annual inspection
choice_d: Prior to the start of any trip, when the trailer(s) are straight
explanation: The manual states, "Mirror adjustment should be checked prior to the start of any trip and can only be checked accurately when the trailer(s) are straight."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.4 Seeing

question: What is a key characteristic of convex ("fisheye") mirrors mentioned in the manual?
choice_a: Everything appears smaller and farther away than it really is
choice_b: They show a narrower area than flat mirrors
choice_c: Objects appear larger and closer than they really are
choice_d: They cannot be used on large vehicles
explanation: The manual states, "Everything appears smaller in a convex mirror than it would if you were looking at it directly. Things also seem farther away than they really are."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.4 Seeing

question: What are the three rules the manual gives for using turn signals?
choice_a: Signal loudly, signal briefly, signal twice
choice_b: Signal early, signal continuously, cancel the signal
choice_c: Signal only at night, signal in curves, signal downhill
choice_d: Signal once, hold the wheel, honk the horn
explanation: The manual lists "Signal early," "Signal continuously," and "Cancel your signal" as the three rules for turns.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.5 Communicating

question: If you must stop on a road or its shoulder, within how many minutes must you put out your emergency warning devices?
explanation: The manual states, "If you must stop on a road or the shoulder of any road, you must put out your emergency warning devices within ten minutes."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.5 Communicating

question: When stopped on a one-way or divided highway, where should warning devices be placed toward approaching traffic?
explanation: The manual states, "Place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward the approaching traffic."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.5 Communicating

question: On a two-lane road carrying traffic in both directions, where should warning devices be placed relative to the vehicle?
choice_a: Within 10 feet of the front/rear corners, and 100 feet behind and ahead of the vehicle
choice_d: Warning devices are not required on two-lane roads
explanation: The manual states to "place warning devices within 10 feet of the front or rear corners to mark the location of the vehicle and 100 feet behind and ahead of the vehicle."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.5 Communicating

question: If a hill or curve blocks the view of your stopped vehicle, warning devices should be placed so drivers can see them from how far away?
explanation: The manual states, "Back beyond any hill, curve, or other obstruction that prevents other drivers from seeing the vehicle within 500 feet."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.5 Communicating

question: At 55 mph, approximately how far does a vehicle travel during braking distance on dry pavement with good brakes?
explanation: The manual states, "At 55 mph on dry pavement with good brakes, [braking distance] can take about 216 feet."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6 Controlling Your Speed

question: At 55 mph, what is the minimum total stopping distance according to the manual?
explanation: The manual states, "At 55 mph, your vehicle will travel a minimum of 419 feet" total stopping distance.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6 Controlling Your Speed

question: According to the manual, doubling your speed from 20 to 40 mph increases the impact and braking distance by how much?
explanation: The manual states, "When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph the impact is 4 times greater. The braking distance is also 4 times longer."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6 Controlling Your Speed

question: Tripling your speed from 20 to 60 mph increases impact and braking distance by how much, per the manual?
explanation: The manual states, "Triple the speed from 20 to 60 mph and the impact and braking distance is 9 times greater."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6 Controlling Your Speed

question: On a wet road, the manual advises reducing speed by about how much compared to dry-road speed?
explanation: The manual states, "Reduce speed by about one-third (e.g., slow from 55 to about 35 mph) on a wet road."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6 Controlling Your Speed

question: On packed snow, how much should you reduce your speed according to the manual?
choice_c: No reduction is needed if you have good tires
explanation: The manual states, "On packed snow, reduce speed by a half, or more."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6 Controlling Your Speed

question: According to the manual, hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as what, if there is a lot of water on the road?
explanation: The manual states, "Hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is a lot of water."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.6 Controlling Your Speed

question: What is the general rule of thumb for following distance below 40 mph, per the manual?
choice_a: Two seconds regardless of vehicle length
choice_b: One second for every 10 feet of vehicle length
choice_c: One car length for every 10 mph
choice_d: Half a second for every 10 feet of vehicle length
explanation: The manual states, "One good rule says you need at least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length at speeds below 40 mph."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.7 Managing Space

question: If you are driving a 40-foot vehicle at speeds above 40 mph, how many seconds of following distance should you leave?
explanation: The manual states, "Over 40 mph, you'd need 5 seconds for a 40-foot vehicle," since you add 1 second to the 4 seconds required below 40 mph.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.7 Managing Space

question: Why does the manual warn against assuming posted bridge and overpass heights are correct?
choice_b: Heights are only estimates and are never accurate
choice_c: Bridge heights change with the seasons due to expansion
choice_d: Re-paving or packed snow may have reduced the clearance since the heights were posted
explanation: The manual states, "Don't assume that the heights posted at bridges and overpasses are correct. Re-paving or packed snow may have reduced the clearances since the heights were posted."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.7 Managing Space

question: What hazard does the manual associate with railroad tracks and drainage channels crossing roads?
choice_a: They can cause the ends of some vehicles to drag or hang up
choice_b: They can cause tire blowouts only
choice_c: They are always marked with warning triangles
choice_d: They only affect vehicles pulling doubles
explanation: The manual states, "Drainage channels across roads can cause the ends of some vehicles to drag... Railroad tracks can also cause problems, particularly when pulling trailers with a low underneath clearance."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.7 Managing Space

question: When making a right turn in a large vehicle that cannot complete the turn without swinging wide, what should you do?
choice_a: Turn wide to the left as you start the turn
choice_b: Turn wide as you complete the turn, keeping the rear close to the curb
choice_c: Stop in the intersection until traffic clears
choice_d: Signal a left turn to confuse following traffic
explanation: The manual states, "Turn wide as you complete the turn. Keep the rear of your vehicle close to the curb. This will stop other drivers from passing you on the right."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.7 Managing Space

question: Before starting a left turn at an intersection, the manual says you should make sure you have done what?
choice_a: Signaled for at least one full block
choice_b: Positioned your vehicle in the leftmost lane
choice_c: Reached the center of the intersection before starting the turn
choice_d: Come to a complete stop regardless of traffic signals
explanation: The manual states, "On a left turn, make sure you have reached the center of the intersection before you start the left turn."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.7 Managing Space

question: According to the manual, what is a "hazard"?
choice_a: Only another vehicle that has already caused a collision
choice_c: A term used solely for construction zones
choice_d: Any road condition or other road user that is a possible danger
explanation: The manual states, "A hazard is any road condition or other road user (driver, bicyclist, pedestrian) that is a possible danger."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.8 Seeing Hazards

question: What vehicles does the manual specifically warn may have drivers who are not used to their limited vision to the sides and rear?
explanation: The manual states, "Rental trucks should be watched carefully. Their drivers are often not used to the limited vision they have to the sides and rear of the truck."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.8 Seeing Hazards

question: The "slow moving vehicle" symbol described in the manual is what shape and color?
choice_b: A red triangle with an orange center
choice_c: A blue circle with a white border
choice_d: An orange square with black stripes
explanation: The manual states, "Some of these will have the 'slow moving vehicle' symbol to warn you. This is a red triangle with an orange center."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.8 Seeing Hazards

question: Which of the following is listed as a clue that a driver may be impaired by alcohol, drugs, or fatigue?
choice_a: Using turn signals well in advance
choice_b: Maintaining a steady speed in the correct lane
choice_c: Stopping at a green light or waiting too long at a stop
choice_d: Keeping windows closed in cold weather
explanation: The manual lists as a clue "Stopping at the wrong time (stopping at a green light, or waiting for too long at a stop)."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.8 Seeing Hazards

question: What have "move-over laws" been enacted to address?
choice_a: Slow drivers blocking the left lane
choice_d: Vehicles struck while stopped at the roadside during incidents or emergencies
explanation: The manual explains that move-over laws address the rising incidence of law enforcement, EMS, fire personnel, and roadside workers "being struck while performing duties at the roadside," requiring drivers to slow and change lanes.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.8 Seeing Hazards

question: According to the Large Truck Crash Causation Study cited in the manual, what percentage of large-truck crashes occurred when the CMV driver was externally distracted?
explanation: The manual states, "8 percent of large-truck crashes occurred when Commercial Motor Vehicle (CMV) drivers were externally distracted and 2 percent... internally distracted."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.9 Distracted Driving

question: Research cited in the manual indicates that talking on a cell phone, even hands-free, saps the brain of what percentage of the energy it would normally devote to safe driving?
explanation: The manual states, "the burden of talking on a cell phone - even if it's hands-free - saps the brain of 39% of the energy it would ordinarily devote to safe driving."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.9 Distracted Driving

question: How much greater are the odds of a safety-critical event for CMV drivers who text while driving, compared to those who don't, according to the manual?
explanation: The manual states, "the odds of being involved in a safety-critical event... is 23.2 times greater for CMV drivers who engage in texting while driving than for those who do not."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.9 Distracted Driving

question: How many convictions of hand-held mobile telephone use while driving a CMV will disqualify your CDL, per the manual?
explanation: The manual states, "Your CDL will be disqualified after two or more convictions of any state law on hand-held mobile telephone use while operating a CMV."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.9 Distracted Driving

question: The manual describes texting as especially dangerous because it involves which combination of distraction?
choice_a: Both physical and mental distraction simultaneously
explanation: The manual states, "Texting is the most alarming distraction because it involves both physical and mental distraction simultaneously."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.9 Distracted Driving

question: How does the manual define "road rage," as distinct from aggressive driving?
choice_a: Driving faster than the posted speed limit
choice_b: Operating a vehicle with the intent of doing harm to others or physically assaulting a driver or vehicle
choice_c: Failing to signal before changing lanes
choice_d: Refusing to yield the right of way
explanation: The manual states, "Road rage is operating a motor vehicle with the intent of doing harm to others or physically assaulting a driver or their vehicle."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.10 Aggressive Drivers/Road Rage

question: What is the first thing the manual recommends doing when confronted by an aggressive driver?
choice_a: Speed up to get ahead of them
choice_c: Make every attempt to get out of their way
explanation: The manual states, "First and foremost, make every attempt to get out of their way."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.10 Aggressive Drivers/Road Rage

question: According to the manual, aggressive driving is defined as operating a vehicle in what manner?
choice_c: A manner focused only on fuel efficiency
choice_d: A selfish, bold, or pushy manner, without regard for the rights or safety of others
explanation: The manual states, "Aggressive driving is the act of operating a motor vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy manner, without regard for the rights or safety of others."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.10 Aggressive Drivers/Road Rage

question: What does the manual suggest doing to reduce stress before and while driving?
choice_c: Speeding up to finish the trip sooner
choice_d: Arguing with dispatch on the radio
explanation: The manual states, "Reduce your stress before and while you drive. Listen to 'easy listening' music."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.10 Aggressive Drivers/Road Rage

question: With low-beam headlights, about how far ahead can you see, according to the manual?
explanation: The manual states, "With low beams you can see ahead about 250 feet."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.11 Driving at Night

question: With high-beam headlights, about how far ahead can you see, according to the manual?
explanation: The manual states, "with high beams about 350-500 feet."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.11 Driving at Night

question: You should dim your headlights within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle or a vehicle you are following?
explanation: The manual states, "Dim your lights within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and when following another vehicle within 500 feet."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.11 Driving at Night

question: According to the manual, getting how much sleep or less triples your risk of a fatigue-related crash?
explanation: The manual states, "Sleep-deprived or fatigued (6 hours of sleep or less triples your risk)."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.11 Driving at Night

question: The manual recommends taking periodic breaks during long trips about how often?
choice_d: Only at the end of the trip
explanation: The manual states, "Take periodic breaks - about every 100 miles or 2 hours during long trips."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.11 Driving at Night

question: What does the manual say is the best advice for driving in fog?
choice_a: Speed up to get through it quickly
choice_b: Use only your high beams for maximum visibility
choice_c: Don't -- pull off the road into a rest area or truck stop until visibility is better
choice_d: Follow closely behind another vehicle's taillights
explanation: The manual states, "The best advice for driving in fog is don't. It is preferable that you pull off the road into a rest area or truck stop until visibility is better."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.12 Driving in Fog

question: If you must drive in fog, what type of lights does the manual recommend using?
choice_c: Four-way flashers only, with headlights off
explanation: The manual states, "Use low-beam headlights and fog lights for best visibility even in daytime."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.12 Driving in Fog

question: What driving behavior does the manual specifically advise avoiding while driving in fog?
choice_d: Watching for vehicles on the side of the road
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to "avoid passing other vehicles" while driving in fog.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.12 Driving in Fog

question: In winter, how can you tell if ice has formed on the road, according to the manual?
choice_b: A lack of spray from other vehicles
choice_c: The road appears darker than usual
explanation: The manual states, "A lack of spray from other vehicles indicates ice has formed on the road."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.13 Driving in Winter

question: Why does the manual advise against using the engine brake or speed retarder on slippery winter roads?
choice_b: It is illegal in winter conditions
choice_c: It can cause the driving wheels to skid on slippery surfaces
explanation: The manual states not to use the engine brake or speed retarder because "they can cause the driving wheels to skid on slippery surfaces."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.13 Driving in Winter

question: What danger does the manual associate with exhaust system leaks in winter driving?
choice_c: Damage to the tires from exhaust heat
choice_d: Carbon monoxide leaking into the vehicle, which can cause sleepiness or death
explanation: The manual states, "Loose connections could permit poisonous carbon monoxide to leak into your vehicle. Carbon monoxide gas will cause you to be sleepy. In large enough amounts it can kill you."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.13 Driving in Winter

question: After driving through deep water, what should you do to your brakes before relying on them fully?
choice_a: Maintain light pressure on the brakes for a short distance to heat them up and dry them out
choice_b: Immediately slam on the brakes at high speed
choice_c: Release the parking brake and coast to dry them naturally
choice_d: Nothing is needed; wet brakes work normally
explanation: The manual states, "When out of the water, maintain light pressure on the brakes for a short distance to heat them up and dry them out."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.13 Driving in Winter

question: In very hot weather, the manual recommends inspecting tires how often?
choice_b: Every two hours or every 100 miles
choice_d: Only at the start and end of the trip
explanation: The manual states, "Inspect the tires every two hours or every 100 miles when driving in very hot weather."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.14 Driving in Very Hot Weather

question: What roadway hazard does the manual describe as occurring when tar "bleeds" to the surface in very hot weather?
choice_a: The road becomes rougher and increases tire wear
choice_b: The road surface hardens and improves traction
choice_d: Tar bleeding only affects unpaved roads
explanation: The manual states, "Spots where tar 'bleeds' to the surface are very slippery."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.14 Driving in Very Hot Weather

question: When should you remove the radiator cap on a pressurized cooling system, according to the manual?
choice_a: As soon as the temperature gauge shows overheating
choice_b: Only while the engine is running
choice_c: Any time, as long as you use gloves
choice_d: Never remove it until the system has cooled
explanation: The manual states, "Never remove the radiator cap or any part of the pressurized system until the system has cooled. Steam and boiling water can spray under pressure and cause severe burns."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.14 Driving in Very Hot Weather

question: At a passive railroad crossing (no traffic control device), who decides whether to stop or proceed?
explanation: The manual states, "This type of crossing does not have any type of traffic control device. The decision to stop or proceed rests entirely in your hands."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.15 Railroad-highway Crossings

question: If there is no white stop line at a cross-buck sign, how close must a vehicle required to stop be to the nearest rail?
choice_a: No closer than 5 feet nor more than 20 feet
choice_b: No closer than 15 feet nor more than 50 feet
choice_c: No closer than 25 feet nor more than 75 feet
choice_d: No closer than 50 feet nor more than 100 feet
explanation: The manual states, "Vehicles that are required to stop must stop no closer than 15 feet or more than 50 feet from the nearest rail of the nearest track."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.15 Railroad-highway Crossings

question: According to the manual, it takes a typical tractor-trailer unit at least how many seconds to clear a single track?
explanation: The manual states, "It takes a typical tractor-trailer unit at least 14 seconds to clear a single track and more than 15 seconds to clear a double track."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.15 Railroad-highway Crossings

question: What does the manual say you should never do while crossing railroad tracks?
choice_c: Keep both hands on the wheel
explanation: The manual states, "Do not shift gears while crossing railroad tracks."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.15 Railroad-highway Crossings

question: What is the manual's proper braking technique when descending a long, steep downgrade?
choice_a: Apply the brakes hard enough to feel a slowdown, then release once speed drops about 5 mph below your safe speed
choice_b: Ride the brakes continuously and lightly the entire way down
choice_c: Never use the brakes at all; rely only on the transmission
choice_d: Pump the brakes rapidly and continuously
explanation: The manual states, "Apply the brakes just hard enough to feel a definite slowdown. When your speed has been reduced to approximately five mph below your 'safe' speed, release the brakes."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.16 Mountain Driving

question: What causes brakes to "fade," according to the manual?
choice_a: Cold weather causing the brake fluid to thicken
choice_b: Excessive heat from using them too much without relying on engine braking
choice_c: Using the engine brake too much
choice_d: Driving too slowly on a downgrade
explanation: The manual states, "Brakes can fade or fail from excessive heat caused by using them too much and not relying on the engine braking effect."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.16 Mountain Driving

question: What is the purpose of escape ramps on steep mountain downgrades?
choice_a: To provide a shortcut for descending faster
choice_b: To allow vehicles to bypass weigh stations
choice_c: To stop runaway vehicles safely without injuring drivers and passengers
choice_d: To provide additional parking for disabled vehicles
explanation: The manual states, "Escape ramps are made to stop runaway vehicles safely without injuring drivers and passengers."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.16 Mountain Driving

question: According to the manual, when should you shift to a low gear before descending a grade?
choice_a: After your speed has already built up on the way down
choice_b: Only if the vehicle has an automatic transmission
choice_c: Gear selection doesn't matter if you use engine braking
